recipes.name: Dry Spice Rub for Lamb or Beef

steps.text: Mix together the paprika, thyme, basil, cumin, and curry powder, if desired, in a small bowl. When ready to use, evenly sprinkle a light coating onto lamb or beef and pat into surface of the meat. For the most flavorful results, season meat and place in a resealable plastic bag; refrigerate 2 hours before cooking.

raw_recipe.headline: Dry Spice Rub for Lamb or Beef
raw_recipe.description: A blend of paprika, dried thyme and basil, cumin, and curry powder, if you choose, makes a flavorful dry rub to season grilled or roasted lamb and beef.
raw_recipe.name: Dry Spice Rub for Lamb or Beef

review.reviewBody: when i rubbed the spices in, i did it with a bit of olive oil. when i cooked it, i added a couple slivers of garlic and a little wine, and then i reduced the sauce to a couple tablespoons. It was really really good.

We liked this, but I did add salt to the rub. Since our family does not care for curry, I substituted some garlic powder and oregano. I placed cut potatoes, carrots, and onion in a bag with some olive oil, a bit of salt, pepper, and dill and then put them in a roasting pan with the roast of beef on top. Served with bacon wrapped grilled asparagus with a tomato and cucumber salad. It was delicious. Grandkids consumed it!!!
I followed this recipe the first time but agree it did need some salt added. Made it a second time but added a little low sodium soy sauce in marinade all were very happy with both
Very good but I’m giving it a 4 because there is no salt. I added salt and pepper and it made a big difference!

Usually I look for a picture of the “chef” to make sure they aren’t white. Because what white person knows how to flavor lamb? But just going off your recipe ingredients I can tell, you come from very European ancestors. So please, update this recipe to at least include salt and pepper. And then contact your nearest poc brethren to fully update this spice list. Sincerely, a white women tired of bland spice rubs.

As the recipe stands, I did not enjoy it. But with one simple tweak it came alive: sea salt. Without the salt, the flavour is plain and hardly comes alive. But once I added salt to the mix, everything was jigging and jiving, and my tongue thanked me greatly! As it is being used on fatty cuts such as lamb, it will not leach out too much liquid. If salt had been added, I would have given this 4-5 stars. Cheers!
This rub was great on the roast I made last night. I added a small amount of salt and fresh ground pepper to the rub, and it was delicious. I'll definitely be using this recipe again!

This was very good. I did add some salt and pepper as suggested by some other reviewers and I feel it did bring out the flavor. I used a mild Jamaican curry. I love Cumin and you just can't go wrong with anything it goes in. :)

This was pretty good, I made up a lot, so I would have more later. I used it this time on lamb chops that I grilled over wood coals. I also let the rub stay on the chops overnight before grilling. Very tasty.

Very good rub, smelled amazing tasted delicious no changes did as per recipe and as instructed seasoned the meat (some thought salt not in recipe - it was as per instructions) so fully deserved 5 stars
This has an incredible smell! I used a sweet paprika in mine, but think next time I'll use a smoky paprika!

I love this recipe, and so does my family. We tried something different, yesterday, though, and put it on a roast, two days ago, then yesterday, we put it in our smoker, with mesquite briquettes. It was so good.
VERY good rub. We added sea salt as well and it was great.

It's also great for pork loin roast! I make this up in bulk and keep it in a labeled airtight jar. I add 1 1/2 tsp salt and 3/4 tsp granulated garlic, and omit the curry (nobody here likes curry) Then I use about 2-3 Tablespoons of the mixture rubbed onto the fat side of the pork roast. When I remember to do it, I poke holes into the roast first, with a fork to let the flavor penetrate. Mmmm good!

Did not care for this spice rub at all. It left very little in the way of flavor. My grilled lamb chops with an acid based marinade have always turned out much better tasting. I wanted to try something new, but the chops were not good with this spice rub.
